transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. And today we're going to go over what I think is
the best preparation that you should be doing leading up to Dragon Wilds September 1.0 launch. But specifically
the launch and the release of the new region Scorned Wilderness. Scorned Wilderness will be out in just over a
month. That's why I wanted to make this guide as early as possible because there are plenty of things that you could be
doing as well as grinding to make the most of your time before we enter Dragon Wilds most diverse region, the Cauldron
Raid. Real quick, before we get into the video, the Golden Gnome finalist voting is now open, guys. It closes on August
14th. I appreciate every single one of you guys. We made it into two categories. I'm very, very honored and I
could not do it without you guys. If you've enjoyed any of the Dragon Wilds content and want to vote for me as well
as plenty of other creators in many different categories, I'm going to be leaving the link down below. I really
appreciate every single one of you guys who's helped me and the channel get this far. Without further ado, let's get
straight into the video. So, this one's going to be very simple, but if you haven't already, most of you guys
probably have, be sure to collect all your Sanguine Earns. I've seen a little bit in the community, some people
thought that this was a healing spot. Basically, you go to it and it gives you a healing boost as you're exploring the
world. But these boost your maximum health by 10. With all the ones currently available, this is going to
bring our health up to around 280. So, be sure you're collecting this. This is basically permanent survivability. Next
up, and I cannot stress this point enough, just this is probably one of my biggest tips that I would go over for
Dragon Wilds. If anyone talked to me about the game, this is one of the biggest points I would give them. Build
up a very, very hefty supply of food as well as drinks. As you guys know, healing and your sustenance, rest as
well as thirst, is all tied to food and drinks now. So, everything is coming from one source. We're going to be
burning through food quite a bit. Now, I made a full guide on food and the best foods you should use based off of the
buffs that are going to accompany your combat style. But just overall, glazed pumpkin sandwiches are still a really
good solid option currently. And I would pair your food with an infusion that matches your combat style. Now, just
like most of us, we probably use all combat styles, but there might be one that you use more heavily, so I would
focus on that infusion specifically. Ferocious infusion reduces stamina used by physical attacks, relentless is for
ranged, arcane is for magic, and evasive infusion reduces the cost of dodging. Get your farming and cooking hats on,
and I would recommend pretty much getting an entire chest filled with food because with Scorned Wilderness being a
raid, we don't know how this area is going to work. We don't know if there's going to be any ability to loadstone out
when we're halfway through. I honestly doubt it, but I don't know. Like, are we going to be able to go through to
certain areas and eventually we'll hit a safe zone where we can teleport back to get more materials. Maybe there's going
to be a merchant inside the raid. I honestly just thought about that as I'm recording this video. Maybe there's
going to be a merchant inside the raid at some point where we can trade certain resources to get extra food items, to
get extra ammo, whatever it may be. That would be insane, actually. I doubt it. We don't know what it's going to be
like, but that would be pretty interesting because either we have to go in with a plethora of food and drinks,
prepare ourselves, or there's going to be some way, shape, or form for us to get more resources as we're progressing
the raid. Next up, this is focusing on getting your weapons as well as armor up to the current power level or as high as
you can. Currently, we can go up to seven. We don't know if we'll eventually go up to eight once we get to the raid.
I'm assuming we will be able to, but it's going to be interesting because this region is going to be completely
different. Who knows if we're going to have upgraded tools in a new set of tools. But as we know, we can take older
masterwork as well as visage weapons, and they can now be brought up to the current power level while retaining the
traits that originally made them special in the first place. Now, a few weapons I
would recommend, but again, this is all based on your own play styles. I recommend the zombie axe. The zombie axe
deals both crush as well as slash damage, which makes it very useful against a wider variety of enemies that
we find out in Ashamfal, and you still will be able to use a shield because it's a one-handed weapon. I also
recommend the Abyssal Whip. I cannot recommend this weapon enough. This is my main weapon early on in early access as
well as now up to this point now that I have it to tier seven. But, this is extremely good, especially if you like
how fast it plays. It's probably one of the strongest and fastest weapons currently in the title. But, keep in
mind, guys, I don't know if this is a bug. The Abyssal Whip does apply bleed, but it does seem like with it's scaling
and getting up to higher power levels, the bleed does not scale with the power level. Again, I don't know if this is a
bug or if this is intended. But, keep that in mind, and I would just recommend the Zombie Axe or the Abyssal Whip. Now,
for two-handed, the Granite Maul is still the king in two-handed weapons. It's raw damage, and it has the ability
to do crush, and it's powerful knockdown special make it arguably the strongest current two-handed weapon in Dragon
Wilds. You could also lean towards the Titan's Wrath. That is a very good two-handed weapon as well. Now, when it
comes to range, especially if we're thinking of a raid, and since we're most likely going to be going against many
different enemies at once, I recommend getting the Dorsal Crossbow up to tier seven. Now, keep in mind this crossbow
can only use bone bolts, but bone bolts apply bleed to specific enemies. This crossbow also offers faster reload, so I
recommend this one. Now, if we're fighting against enemies that can't receive bleed, I recommend the Bluerite
Crossbow as a really strong alternative. Now, in terms of just standard bows, the Bow of Elidinis is still very, very
excellent. It is by far my favorite bow in the game. But, just keep in mind it does have water damage and the AoE
special ability. So, if you're going against enemies that are strong to water, it might not be that versatile in
the raid. Now, there's also a strange one that is worth mentioning. The Hunter's Stag Bow can reach extremely
high damage at tier seven. Now, I suspect that the scaling is unintended. We have seen this in the past with bows.
We did get a massive nerf to bows overall, which I think was great. I thought bows were super fun in the past.
They're still fun, but it did receive a nerf and I honestly think the hunter stag bow is going to be one of those
weapons that gets a nerf when they do the combat overhaul. But overall, I do not recommend it as your main range
weapon. I still would go with a bow of elitist because if it does get a nerf, you're going to be wasting your
ascension course to level up that weapon. So overall for range, I recommend the Dorgensen crossbow, the
blue right crossbow, the bow of elitist as well as the hunter stag bow. Now in terms of staffs, honestly, it's kind of
self preference, but there is one that reigns supreme across the board and this is a necromancer staff. It is currently
the highest DPS magic staff after ascending it to tier seven. Now it's original base trait is simply increased
damage in exchange for lower durability. So you're going to be losing durability a lot faster with this weapon. So keep
that in mind. But we have magical men, so when we are in the raid, we can easily repair this weapon, but it will
break a lot faster than other staffs in the title. On top of that, one of my favorite staffs in the game is the staff
of light and then in my opinion, this is the next best general option for you. Again, it's all about play style, it's
all about preference, whichever one you like more. And then next up, we have the Zamorakian staff, which is also very
useful for fire builds because it increases burning damage, but reduces air, water, and earth spell damage. So
you're going to be going for a debuff with the other elements, but getting a buff for fire specifically. And keep in
mind guys, really quickly, you can bring multiple weapons into the raid. So you can have multiple weapons and depending
on what's going on and what's happening, what kind of enemies you're encountering, maybe an enemy is strong
to fire, you just won't use the Zamorakian staff, you could switch to necromancer or the staff of light. It's
totally an option. It's not necessary. But I know I did that with the fight cave just to ensure my weapons wouldn't
break. The last staff I want to go over is the Pharaoh staff. This is still a great staff. It does not have as much
base damage, but with having the Kalphite minion and being able to spawn it, we do know the special attack bar is
going to be introduced to the game, so we will be able to understand the timing of it. Currently, it's kind of weird. We
do believe it's working off of the timing that the special attack bar is going to have once it's actually
introduced, but I'm not 100% sure on that yet. But overall for me, the Pharaoh staff was very, very good and
very versatile during the fight caves cuz I would summon the Calfight and I would run away and all the enemies would
aggro the Calfight and it gave me big windows to just dish out a ton of damage. Basically, what I would do is
summon the Calfight, run some distance away, and then use the bow of Aledannus' special ability and just rain water
damage down on them. So, that is workable, too. Again, guys, I keep saying it, but it's all about
preference, it's all about playstyle. Even if it's the highest DPS weapon in the title, it may not be that versatile
for you because you may play a certain way and your strengths may benefit from using a different weapon. So, just keep
that in mind. The next thing I would prioritize is accumulating a ton of ammo as well as plenty of runes. As we know
with the recent update, we can now switch ammo as well as runes on the fly, which is absolutely fantastic. Keep in
mind, if you are using the Dorgesh-Kaan bow, you will not be able to use any other bow other than bone, so just keep
that in mind if that's the one you go for. This is simple. When it comes to arrows, you're just going to want to use
the tier seven adamant arrows. But I recommend you making plenty of stacks of every kind of arrow type. So, barbed
arrows, which will apply bleed, the poisoned arrows, which will apply poison, fire arrows, as well as normal
arrows. Be sure you have a wide variety as well as a wide range of different ammo types in your arsenal cuz you're
going to be able to dish more damage against certain enemy types. Now, honestly, when I was making this guide,
I thought of this and this is another huge tip that I would say even for beginners is level agility as high as
you can go. Agility is probably one of the biggest things I would work on right now because you're going to be able to

like the double jump, the aerial dash, the double aerial dash, the the recovery, the recall spell, which could

train a lot of agility in different areas around Ashton Fall. I know that might sound weird. You could do courses,

Scorned Wilderness is going to be very different than any other region. It's been described as a raid style push with

simple, but this is what I do before each update is I make basically a forward operating base, just a small
